title: Reel claim check (Instagram/Facebook reel posted 2026-10-23, captioned about data-center water and the UT Austin paper)

paper.citation: Katakam, A., Arzumanyan, M., Lin, S., Bahadur, V. System-scale design and analysis of desalination systems for meeting water needs of data centers. Water Research, vol. 308, article 126748 (online 2026-08-17; vol. 308 Part B).
paper.abstract_finding: Abstract and press coverage only; the full text was not accessed. The paper compares desalination-based water supply scenarios for data centers, introduces a Sustainable Water Use Index (SWUI), and reports that for a Longview, Texas case, brackish-groundwater supply with two-stage reverse osmosis scored best of the three scenarios studied.

press.note: Anthropocene Magazine, Oct 2026 (source of the '8 billion gallons per day' figure; not supported by primary sources)

claims.claim: The Permian generates roughly 8 billion gallons of produced water every day.
claims.evidence: Texas Tech/TAWC (2025) gives about 20 million bbl/day (840 million gal/day) and B3 Insight about 20.7 million bpd for 2025 (869 million gal/day). The Railroad Commission gives about 24 million bbl/day for all of Texas (1.0 billion gal/day). 8 billion gal/day would be about 190 million bbl/day.
claims.label: ANALYTIC ASSESSMENT

claims.claim: That is about 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools every day.
claims.verdict: CONSISTENT with 0.84 billion gal/day, inconsistent with 8 billion
claims.evidence: 840 million gallons / 660,430 gallons per 2,500 m3 pool is about 1,270 pools. 8 billion gallons would be about 12,100 pools. The reel's own pool figure matches the lower number.
claims.label: ANALYTIC ASSESSMENT

claims.claim: A large data center can use up to 5 million gallons a day.
claims.evidence: EESI states that a large data center can consume up to 5 million gallons per day. LBNL reports US data centers directly consumed about 17.4 billion gallons (66 billion litres) in 2023, which is an average, not a per-site maximum.
claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.claim: Longview scored the best of anywhere tested.
claims.evidence: The UT release and abstract describe Longview as the best of the three supply scenarios examined in a Longview case study (brackish groundwater with two-stage RO), not the best location among sites. This atlas's MODELED regional screen does not rank Longview first (see Siting).
claims.label: ANALYTIC ASSESSMENT

claims.claim: The study is in Water Research 'this fall'.
claims.evidence: The article is dated online 2026-08-17 (summer) and is in volume 308; UT's press release followed on Oct 8, 2026.
claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.claim: Context (UT release, not a reel claim): disposal space for produced water may run short.
claims.evidence: The UT release quotes co-author Bahadur on running out of disposal space by as early as 2030. That is a researcher's projection, not a regulatory finding. B3 Insight reports about 2.8 million bpd already moved from New Mexico to Texas for disposal.
claims.label: OBSERVED

claims.claim: The Texas Attorney General is scrutinising data center water use.
claims.evidence: Press releases dated Sep 24 and Oct 15, 2026 describe an AG investigation of data center developments that did not respond to the TWDB water-use survey.
claims.label: OBSERVED

note: Figures verified on 2026-11-04 against the linked pages. The reel itself was read from its caption metadata only.
